properties.decision:
Recorded as brainstorming on 2026-09-19 from flo2 F18 (as corrected by its author) and F22, not as a proposal. One question because both halves are the same tool's interface and the same consumer pays for both, and they would be decided together.

HALF ONE — RETURN THE PIECES. `{status: needs_llm, prompts: [...], gap: {id, title, why}}`. The server already holds title and description as separate values and formats them together at detect.rs:1553; this returns what it had before it joined them. A consumer wanting a phrased question follows phase two as designed; a consumer wanting context for its own model turn reads `gap.why` and never touches prose. It is the only thing standing between flo2 and the black-box rule, and the reporter sizes it at one field.
COUNTER, such as it is: it widens the reply for every caller to serve one, and a reply that carries both the composed form and its parts invites a consumer to depend on both.

HALF TWO — TAKE A KEY. Options: accept `gap_id` as a string alternative; or mark the object's other fields explicitly ignored in the schema; or put the echo caveat on the PARAMETER's own description, where a caller reading the type will meet it. Today the caveat is on the tool's description and the parameter reads 'A GapCandidate previously returned by detect_gaps', so the shape says hand me the finding while the semantics say hand me a key.

⭐ THE THIRD OPTION THE REPORTER FOUND WHILE COMPLAINING, and it may be better than either: their redundant detect_gaps call is also how a stale chip is refused with 'that is no longer open'. If gap_to_prompt answered a VANISHED gap with a distinguishable refusal, the consumer could drop the extra call and still be correct. Taking an id closes the cost; a distinguishable refusal closes the cost AND the correctness question, and is the only one that removes the recomputation rather than making it cheaper to avoid.
properties.name: OPEN — should gap_to_prompt return the gap's pieces beside the prompt it builds from them, and should it take a key rather than an object it only reads a key from?
